If sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) in the last 5 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture momentum.

If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) in the last 5 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overcorrection.

If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-cycle (last 3 days), reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending upward, cap upward movement at +1.5% for late horizon (16–30 days) to prevent overextension.

If sentiment is neutral and forecast is trending downward, cap downward movement at -1.5% for late horizon (16–30 days) to avoid premature sell-off.

If sentiment is bullish but forecast is below 72.0, add 0.8–1.2% to forecast for late horizon (25–30 days) to align with sentiment-driven price breakout.
